scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service charge 34 days after cancellation, exceeding the standard 30-day window due to travel.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Emily Baker and I'm 31. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, so you want a refund for a charge from 34 days ago? I see. I'm not sure if I can do that since it's past the window. What is your account number?
My account number is 8849201. I really hope you can help, it was just a few days over the limit.
I have your account up. You said you canceled 34 days ago, but I need you to tell me the date you canceled again? I'm not seeing the cancellation request clearly in the logs.
I canceled on October 1st, as I mentioned. Can you see the transaction ID ending in 9928? That's the one I'm referring to.

Yeah, I see it. Look, our policy is 30 days, that's just how it is. Since you're asking for an exception, I'm just going to send this over to the billing department to look at. They handle these things.
Oh, so you can't process it yourself? How long will that take?
I don't know, they'll email you. I've opened the case for you. Is there anything else?

escalation_reason: Agent lacked confidence in policy exceptions and offloaded the request to the billing department instead of exercising available discretion.

judge_scores.justification: The agent showed poor resolution effort by immediately escalating the request to billing without exercising any discretion or attempting to help within their authority. The conversation also lacked efficiency and empathy, requiring the customer to repeat information and receiving a curt response regarding policy limits.
